_what: A list is a record of `list_kind` whose `row_type_field` names its rows' kind after `row_kind_prefix` and whose `fields_field` holds its fields, as the list tool's declared_by says; a read of a row works out its computed fields from them, reading at most `most_lists` lists. How the record store runs formula fields, trigger rules and workflow runs (src/rule_bindings/rules_and_runs.rs), ported from Trillion's src/rules-over-records.mjs, src/workflow-definition-runner.mjs, src/automations.mjs (changed, evaluate, keep, runPayload) and src/workflows.mjs (start). The record kinds these rules and runs read and write are not here: they are the `kinds_section` of the account's installed record model (the tool that keeps the rules declares it: `rule`, the kind of the account's rule rows, each holding the trigger engine's own rule (match_condition, dispatch); `outcome`, `run`, `recipe`, `send`, and `own`), so with that tool not installed no rule runs. `rule_partition` and `workflow_partition` are the partitions the rules and runs are handed, as Trillion's automations passed its store id and its workflows 'person'. `own` are the kinds of the rows these rules and runs write (their outcomes and runs) and of the rules themselves: a write of one is never handed to the rules as a change, as Trillion kept its rule runs unwatched and reset its rule cache on a rule write. `run` is the kind of a workflow run's row and `run_id_prefix` the start of its id; `recipe` is the kind of the row that holds a workflow's engine definition under `recipe_definition_field`. `rule_run_prefix` starts the id of each row the trigger engine writes about its own sends, kept as the kind the rules name, or `outcome` when it names none. `most_rules` bounds how many rule rows one write reads; `run_id_hex` is how many hex digits of the run identity name a run (Trillion: identityOf(...).slice(3, 27)); `rule_run_hex` the hex digits of a rule-run row's address hash (Trillion shortHash). `write_ask` is the name a workflow step asks under when its effect is a write of the account's own records (the generic records write: Trillion's run_tool step, whose tool's effect was a records write, workflows.mjs answerFromTool): its input's `records` are each `{id, type, set?, add?, remove?, expected?}`, applied on the same held transaction once the run passes, compare-and-set on the version read there; `most_step_writes` bounds how many records one run writes. What a run's write steps wrote is handed to the rules again, as Trillion's store handed every write to its automations, for at most `most_rule_rounds` rounds of rules on one records write (the first round is the write itself). `send` is the kind of the row a rule's send to a tool (`then.tool_id`) is kept as, id `send_prefix` + the hex of its identity, for the wake runner (src/wake.rs `sends`) to take. `shipped_rules` is where the rules that ship with the deploy are read: each installed tool folder's `file` (`rows` of it, every row with `id_field` a rule), compiled from their plain words (src/rule_bindings/rules_and_runs/shipped_rules.rs) and read beside the account's own rule rows, never written into its store (src/records/shipped_defaults.rs invariant 1); `schedule_id_field` marks a row of the same file that is a schedule, not a rule: it is read by the wake (`shipped_schedules`); `change_field` is the field a changed record's value carries `{ kind, id, record }` under for them to bind, beside the record's own fields that the account's own rules bind; `max_bytes` bounds one file. `shipped_recipes` is where the workflows that ship with the deploy are read: each installed tool folder's `dir`, every `.json` file there, the `payload_field` of each of its `rows` a recipe with `id_field` (src/rule_bindings/rules_and_runs/shipped_recipes.rs), read beside the account's own recipe rows, never written; `agent_ask` is how an ask answered by an AI is handed over: an ask named `ask_prefix` (and the AI after it, or `to_input_field` of its input) becomes one `job_kind` record, id `id_prefix` and the hex of its handoff key (its input's `once_per_input_field`, else the run and step), holding its `job_input_field` text with the `details_input_fields` of its input, `said_input_field` as its label, status `waiting`, `priority_input_field` as its priority and the run and step it answers (`run_field`, `step_field`); once the job's status is one of `done`, its `result_field` is the ask's answer and the run goes on, and one of `failed` fails the run with its `error_field`; `recipe_steps` is how a recipe row with an empty definition is read: the rows of `kind` (or `kind` after `row_kind_prefix`, as a list's rows are kept) whose ids are `row_kind_prefix`, `kind`, a colon, the recipe's name and `id_separator` and whose `recipe_field` names the recipe, at most `most_steps`, in `order_field` order, each with its `text_fields` read from JSON text. An account's own recipe row is the `recipe` kind's row named by the workflow id or by its name after the first colon, or the row of the person's list of workflows, that kind after `row_kind_prefix`.
